March 10, 2025

Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and fellow members of the Joint
Standing Committee on State and Local Government. I am Representative Randy Greenwood, proudly representing my friends and neighbors in Litchfield,
Monmouth, and my hometown in Wales, both in Androscoggin and K6l11'l6bC Counties. I am here today to present L.D. 616, "An Act to Provide Funding to the
Maine Semiquincentennial Commission to Commemorate the United States of
America's 250th Birthday in 2026 and to express my strong support for this bill.
The last 249 years of American history are filled with fascinating, inspiring and thought-provoking stories. That's true on the grand, national scale, and it is true
down to the very local scale of the towns in my district -- and in all of yours. Did you know that the town of Monmouth is named in tribute to Continental Army
General Henry Dearborn, who fought side-by-side with George Washington at the
Battle of Monmouth in New Jersey in 1778? After the war, he settled near to here
on land in an area he'd first encountered on a 1775 trek to Quebec to attack British
forces. He helped to found a local school and eventually was the inspiration to the name of the town at its incorporation in 1792.
America's history is filled with stories like this, and LD 616 will help local
institutions tell them. The bill provides one-time funding of $250,000 for the Maine Semiquincentennial Commission to pay for public programs as a state match to private funding. This state match funding will help enterprising local institutions supplement private fundraising in order to help them share our country's soon-to-be 250 years of history with the public.
As a lover of history and the towns of my district, I encourage you to join me in supporting LD 616.
Thank you for the opportunity to introduce this bill and I would be happy to
answer any questions you may have.

Maine is well prepared for these anniversary events. In 2023, Maine Chapter Law 126 established "a Commission to Commemorate the 25 0"` Anniversary of the Founding of the
United States." The Maine Semiquincentemiial Commission has been working hard to develop and coordinate the commemoration of the 250th amiiversary of the founding of the United States of America, through educational and historical events, activities, and programs throughout the State. This anniversary presents a rare opportunity to share the whole history of our nation and further strive towards a more perfect union. It also offers a chance to transform and strengthen the history field, preparing it to thrive for decades to come, especially here in Maine.

To guide its work, the Commission developed three foundational pillars.
Connect: Uniting Maine's Stories with America's Legacy - Foster a sense of community and shared heritage through collaborative events and
discussions.

Share: Illuminating Maine's Legacy in America's Story ~ Provide engaging and informative programs that highlight Maine's role in American
`
history and the broader national narrative.

Learn: Examining Maine's Role in America's Ongoing Journey - Encourage lifelong learning and curiosity about our past, present, and future.
Maine is one of 56 U.S. states and territories with a commission that helps coordinate activities and programming for the upcoming Semiquincentennial. Our Commission plays an important role in determining the scope and direction of the commemoration, interfacing with the U.S. Semiquincentennial Commission and America250, recognizing local programming, and, with your suppoit, providing necessary funding.
As part of our community outreach, staff conducted an online survey shared with hundreds of organizations throughout Maine to better understand the current state of organizations' planning efforts. One result stands out: our communities need financial and volunteer support to ensure programming and events surrounding this national milestone are successful. This bill will allow the Semiquincentemiial Commission to meet these community needs by providing funding that will match private dollars.
I urge this committee to recognize the importance of honoring and commemorating the 250"` anniversary of the founding of our nation, helping all Mainers explore and learn from our shared American history by supporting L.D. 616. This will allow our museums, historical societies, and other organizations to demonstrate their value to communities across the state by offering relevant, creative, and sustainable programs and services during the Semiquincentennial and
beyond. This concludes my testimony. I would be happy to answer questions.
